Does the team monitor the extent to which requests (either via the portal or otherwise) result in the publication of the requested data?

column4: The portal team is part of the process / procedure that informs the institutions of the respective request, as this is not an automated process. As such, the response is also monitored. As part of the new Law on open data, the public institutions will have to report yearly on the number of requests they received directly and how many have resulted in publication of requested data (this will be implemented from 2023 on).

column2: 2.2 Portal usage

Do you monitor the portal's traffic (e.g. in terms of number of unique visitors, visitor profiles, percentage of machine traffic, number of downloads according to the number of datasets etc.)? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, which tool(s) do you use?

Do you run analytics on API usage?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly (1) describe your process and (2) how you use the insights to improve the portal

Besides monitoring portal traffic, do you perform any further activities to better understand the behaviour and needs of users of your portal (e.g. web analytics, surveys, or analysis of social media feeds)?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) specify the activities and explain (2) how they help you understand user needs
column7: We are also now conducting an online survey on User satisfaction (available as a pop-up on the portal and disseminated through mailing lists/open data stewards): https://forms.gle/6rMkWhmxLfMyd4nq5. The survey enables us to have a better picture on who the users are (public sector, academia, private sector etc.), their reasons for accessing the portal and type of engaggement and, most importantly, as we are planning a portal update, it helps us prioritise the needs for new or improved features and functionalities

column2:
Do you used the insights about portal usage and about the behaviour and needs of portal users to improve the portal accordingly?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please explain your process for improving the portal based on user insights and feedback
* If relevant, kindly highlight some improvements made in the past year
column7: We are also now conducting an online survey on User satisfaction (available as a pop-up on the portal and disseminated through mailing lists/open data stewards): https://forms.gle/6rMkWhmxLfMyd4nq5. The survey enables us to have a better picture on who the users are (public sector, academia, private sector etc.), their reasons for accessing the portal and type of engaggement and, most importantly, as we are planning a major portal update, it helps us prioritise the needs for new or improved features and functionalities and will feed into the project documentation.

column7: The portal is promoted through webinars, public meetings (academia, private sector), dedicated information sessions (students), mentions on open data/portal in new guidelines for the digitalisation of public services (central and local public service providers), presentations and updates in the national Committee on e-government and red-tape Reduction etc.

column7: Through the Search Console module of Google Analytics. The most searched keywords match the most consulted categories /datasets (in terms of either the subject or the publisher of the dataset).

2.3 Data provision

To what degree do public sector data providers contribute data to the portal? 

For Explanation:
*Please describe what is the agreed approach.
* If less than the majority of data providers, please briefly explain why (e.g. technical incompatibilities, governance aspects, low awareness etc.).
column3: the majority of public sector data providers
column4: Although all public sector data providers are encouraged to contribute to the national data portal, there are several institutions that choose to publish on their own portals that were previously designed for their specific data (Ministry of Finance – transparenta-bugetara.gov.ro, National Statistics Institute - http://statistici.insse.ro:8077/tempo-online/#/pages/tables/insse-table, National Cadastre Agency - http://geoportal.gov.ro/Geoportal_INIS/). These have not been included yet in the national open data portal.

column2: 2.4 Portal sustainability

Does the national portal have a strategy to ensure its sustainability?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) provide the URL to this document and (2) describe the main measures to keep the portal running in the long-term and continue to serve its audience
column7:
There is currently a dedicated funding line for open data from EU funds (Smart Growth, Digitalisation and Financial Instruments Programme 2021-2027): https://oipsi.gov.ro/lansarea-apelului-pocidif-aferent-actiunii-2-2-1-e-guv-in-administratia-institutiile-publice-masura-3-dezvoltarea-de-platforme-informatice-alimentate-cu-datele-generate-de-ad/.
As the main beneficiary of this funding is the development of the national open data portal (according to the Applicant's Guide), the Secretariat General of the Government has initiated preparation for a project submission to update and improve the portal. As part of this, we are conducting an initial analysis that will include proposed sustainability measures for the portal, both in terms of funding, uptake and technical, taking into consideration this update project.
